MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 22, 2026

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR ZERUNYAN called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Administrative Services Director Fernando Estrada.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Stegura

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Donald M. Davis
  Community Dev. & PW Director Jeannie Naughton
  Administrative Services Director Fernando Estrada
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING OCTOBER 2026 "BREAST CANCER AWARENESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR ZERUNYAN declared October 2026 as “Breast Cancer Awareness Month,” and
presented the proclamation to Evelyn Calip, Breast Oncology Nurse & Founder of Non-Profit
Evelyn’s Breast Friends Forever (BFF).

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS
  BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF AUGUST 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF AUGUST 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 8, 2026

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 22, 2026
 E.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 16,
  2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 260213
  PROPOSED AMENDMENTS TO TITLE 17 (ZONING) OF THE MUNICIPAL CODE
  ADDING OR AMENDING 10 CHAPTERS

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take public
  testimony; 3) Discuss Ordinance No. 763; 4) Continue the Public Hearing to October
  13, 2026; and 5) Introduce for first reading Ordinance No. 763, amending seven existing
  chapters and adding three chapters to the Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code, and
  determining the code amendments are exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act.

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material), and introduced City Attorney Don Davis, who went through the
proposed Ordinance updates.

City Attorney Davis presented proposed updates to 10 zoning code chapters: three new
chapters and seven revised chapters. The changes are intended to streamline and clarify
administrative procedures, reduce duplication, align provisions with state law, and make the
code easier for the public to understand. The Planning Commission recommended approval
after one change based on its feedback.

Key proposals included:
  • Establishing uniform application, review, decision, expiration, amendment,
  revocation, and appeal procedures.
  • Consolidating public notice requirements, including 10- or 20-day notice periods and
  mailing notice in some cases.
  • Clarifying the Community Development Director’s duties, code interpretation process,
  and enforcement options.
  • Updating nonconforming use rules, variance findings, and conditional use permit
  findings; most special use permit changes are procedural.
  • Extending the City Council’s review period for Planning Commission decisions from
  20 to 30 days.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  open the public hearing.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING TO OCTOBER 13, 2026, AND
  INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING ORDINANCE NO. 763, AMENDING
  SEVEN EXISTING CHAPTERS AND ADDING THREE CHAPTERS TO THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE, AND DETERMINED THAT
  THE CODE AMENDMENTS ARE EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 22, 2026
 Assistant to the City Manager Slawson read Ordinance No. 763 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  WILDFIRE CAMERA MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE
  CITIES OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES, ROLLING HILLS, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES,
  AND PALOS VERDES ESTATES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Memorandum of Understanding
  between the City of Rancho Palos Verdes, Rolling Hills, Rolling Hills Estates, and
  Palos Verdes Estates to manage and fund the established Wildfire Detection Camera
  System.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE
  CITY OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES, ROLLING HILLS, ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, AND PALOS VERDES ESTATES TO MANAGE AND FUND THE
  ESTABLISHED WILDFIRE DETECTION CAMERA SYSTEM.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT: Stegura

B.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: SB 1383 RECOVERED
  ORGANIC WASTE PRODUCT PROCUREMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve Waste Management’s proposal
  to procure 376 tons of qualifying compost, equivalent to the City’s 648-ton 2026
  recovered organic waste procurement target, for a total cost of $5,640, with
  procurement completed by November 1, 2026, to remain eligible for reimbursement
  through the SB 1383 Local Assistance Grant Program; and 2) Direct City staff to
  evaluate future procurement options, including the five-year procurement target
  option for the 2027-2031 compliance period and community-based composting
  opportunities involving local schools and the George F Canyon Nature Center, to
  determine how these approaches could help satisfy the City’s procurement
  requirements while providing community and educational benefits.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ discussed whether the 648-ton procurement requirement
applies to raw organic material or finished compost. Assistant City Manager Davis clarified
that the requirement is based on the converted end product and explained that a long-term
City program could use a combination of options, including community composting, wood
chips, landscape waste, and eligible composting equipment, to offset a portion of the annual
procurement target. She also noted that processing the full amount internally would likely be
impractical and cost prohibitive and recommended further evaluating feasible options and
their cost benefits for a potential multi-year program.

Discussion ensued about the extensive SB 1383 reporting requirements. Staff explained
that the City is responsible for annual reporting to CalRecycle, with Waste Management
providing data and inspection assistance and consultant City Green assisting with
development of the required implementation record.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER asked whether horse manure could contribute toward the
City’s compliance efforts; staff noted that its composition, including wood shavings, creates
challenges for composting and anaerobic digestion, but opportunities for its beneficial use
continue to be explored.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 22, 2026
 Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) APPROVE WASTE MANAGEMENT’S PROPOSAL TO PROCURE 376
  TONS OF QUALIFYING COMPOST, EQUIVALENT TO THE CITY’S 648-TON
  2026 RECOVERED ORGANIC WASTE PROCUREMENT TARGET, FOR A
  TOTAL COST OF $5,640, WITH PROCUREMENT COMPLETED BY
  NOVEMBER 1, 2026, TO REMAIN ELIGIBLE FOR REIMBURSEMENT
  THROUGH THE SB 1383 LOCAL ASSISTANCE GRANT PROGRAM; AND 2)
  DIRECT CITY STAFF TO EVALUATE FUTURE PROCUREMENT OPTIONS,
  INCLUDING THE FIVE-YEAR PROCUREMENT TARGET OPTION FOR THE
  2027-2031  COMPLIANCE  PERIOD  AND  COMMUNITY-BASED
  COMPOSTING OPPORTUNITIES INVOLVING LOCAL SCHOOLS AND THE
  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER, TO DETERMINE HOW THESE
  APPROACHES COULD HELP SATISFY THE CITY’S PROCUREMENT
  REQUIREMENTS WHILE PROVIDING COMMUNITY AND EDUCATIONAL
  BENEFITS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT: Stegura

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 764 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 10.44 REGARDING THE REGULATION
  OF BICYCLES, ELECTRIC BICYCLES AND OTHER MOTORIZED DEVICES, AND
  CHAPTER 10.46 REGARDING THE REGULATION OF WHEELED VEHICLES ON
  PUBLIC EQUESTRIAN PATHS AND TRAILS

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct the second reading and adopt
  Ordinance No. 764.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Written public testimony was received from Brian More and Darren Eades.

City Attorney Davis addressed public comments regarding the proposed amendments to
Chapter 10.46, explaining that the limited exceptions for wheeled devices on equestrian trails
are intended to support equestrian uses, such as hay deliveries, and would not unduly burden
the City’s trail easements. He noted that reasonable use is implied and that the ordinance
provides sufficient standards to address potential abuses.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN agreed that any unreasonable or excessive use should be addressed
through enforcement rather than further amendments to the ordinance.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONDUCTED THE SECOND READING AND ADOPTED ORDINANCE NO.
  764.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT: Stegura

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson read Ordinance No. 764 by title.

B.  QUARTERLY WORK PLAN UPDATE

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 22, 2026
 City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), highlighting
progress on several priority projects. The George F Canyon Nature Center remains on
schedule for summer 2027 completion; Phase 1 of the Palos Verdes Drive North/Dapplegray
School intersection project remains under construction with traffic and pedestrian access
maintained; and work continues on the Peter Weber Equestrian Center restroom project. He
also provided updates on the equestrian user fee study, landmark protection ordinance, zoning
code amendments, horse census, Pavement Management System, and sidewalk assessment.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

The City Attorney reported that, due to the increasing complexity of planning matters
resulting from changes in State law, and at the City Manager’s request, his office will now
provide legal counsel at Planning Commission meetings. He stated that Robert Khuu, a
partner with the firm, will attend the meetings for the foreseeable future. This will provide
continuity and ensure the City Attorney’s office stays informed about planning matters before
they come before the City Council.

11.  CITY COUNCIL / REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reported that California Contract Cities Association adopted
its annual budget, with the City’s annual dues increasing by $100. The Legislative Committee
continues to monitor and advocate on legislation affecting local control, particularly related to
transportation, development, and ADUs, while also supporting beneficial legislation such as
wildfire-related measures.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF thanked staff for a successful City Celebration, which had a great
turnout and participation from neighboring communities. She also reported that the City will be
represented at the upcoming Cal Cities Annual Conference, including the Los Angeles County
Division luncheon.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER noted that the Traffic & Safety Committee meeting will take
place tomorrow night.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that he will be attending the Los Angeles County Division luncheon
tomorrow.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

None.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked staff for their efforts in making the 69th Annual City
Celebration a success, highlighting the strong family participation and the City’s unique
equestrian and semi-rural character. He also congratulated the Sheriff’s Department on its
volleyball tournament victory and expressed enthusiasm for continuing the friendly rivalry
next year.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting at 8:18 p.m. to Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a regular City Council meeting.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 22, 2026
 Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Frank V. Zerunyan, Mayor
